newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks up, led by conglomerate flagships.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks up, led by conglomerate flagships.

text.p: Colombian stocks rose as foreign funds stepped in to snap up shares in the flagship companies of some of the country's major conglomerates.
Bogota's IBB index rose 0.65 percent to 1,076.66 amid a 2 billion peso trade, while Medellin's IBOMED index rose 0.41 percent to 16,664.28 in a 3.8 billion peso trade.
"Foreign funds were looking for Bavaria stocks and others from the Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate because of the strength they showed in 1996," a Bogota broker said.
He added that foreign funds were keen to invest in emerging markets given recent falls in Europe and on Wall Street.
Brewing giant Bavaria, head of the Santo Domingo conglomerate, rose 2.57 percent to to a historic high of 7,180 in Bogota and 2.84 percent to 7,199 in Medellin.
Banco Bancoquia rose 1.56 percent to 3,240 in Bogota and 4.69 percent to 3,350 in Medellin.
Supermarket chain Cadenalco, head of the Sindacato Antioqueno retail sector, rose 2.15 percent to 899 in Bogota and remained unchanged at 900 in Medellin.
Banco de Bogota, owned by finance magnate Luis Carlos Sarmiento, rose 0.72 percent to 6,100 in Bogota and 0.79 percent to the same price in Medellin.
